t: You're at Brompton Road, a disused station on the Piccadilly line. It sits between Knightsbridge and South Kensington, and trains no longer stop here. The man who designed it was Leslie Green, an English architect. He is best known for the stations he designed across central London in the first decade of the twentieth century. They have distinctive oxblood red faïence blocks, pillars and semi-circular first-floor windows, and patterned tiled interiors in the Modern Style. Green died in 1908, aged only thirty-three, so this is the work of a short career. Look for that red glazed front and the rounded upper windows.
